input.rationale: Request an execution for the gap the current account still lists and for the second half of the question. The three receipts so far cover the single-voter remainder on both routes and the unanswered request in the multi-voter remainder with the quorum options off; this harness measures the same removal when the remainder has two voters and only PreVote is enabled, where the singleton shortcut cannot apply, and records what the caller ends up with. The harness was built against the captured source and its intended sequence appears in a scratch copy of the module: the removed leader takes the request into readOnly.unconfirmedReads and broadcasts two heartbeats instead of taking the shortcut, steps down after one tick when it learns of the new term, and the accepted request then disappears with no answer and no refusal (read_states 0, unconfirmed_reads 0, refused_to_caller false).

scope.description: Observe a ReadIndex request delivered to a leader whose removal the application applied and whose reduced configuration still has two voters, with PreVote enabled and CheckQuorum disabled: node 1 is elected in {1,2,3}, the application proposes and applies the committed removal of node 1 on all three nodes, the two remaining voters elect node 2 and it commits an entry the removed leader never sees, the read is delivered to node 1, one heartbeat tick of node 1 is delivered and its messages pumped, and the state of the request is then recorded.
assumptions: Three voters {1,2,3} with PreVote enabled on every node and CheckQuorum disabled; the election tick is 10 and the heartbeat tick is 1; node 1 is elected with a real MsgHup/MsgPreVote/MsgVote round.

The application applies the committed removal of node 1 on all three nodes, so node 1 keeps leading a configuration of voters (2 3) under the default StepDownOnRemoval=false while node 2 becomes leader of the same configuration at the next term.
The read is delivered to node 1 after node 2 has committed, then one heartbeat tick of node 1 is delivered and its messages are pumped through the network.
excluded: Snapshots, asynchronous storage writes, and any state machine behind the read index.

experiment.prefix: Elect node 1 in {1,2,3} with PreVote enabled, apply the committed removal of node 1 on all three nodes, elect node 2 in {2,3} and commit one proposal, deliver MsgReadIndex to node 1 and read its emitted messages, deliver one heartbeat tick of node 1 and pump its messages, then record the request's fate and node 1's state.
experiment.requirement: A ReadIndex answer must let the application serve a linearizable read (raft.go:233-244 and README.md:27-32 state that ReadOnlySafe achieves linearizability by communicating with the quorum, and node.go:218-224 states that once the application advances past the returned read index, linearizable reads issued before the request can be processed safely) and requests that cannot be answered are the caller's to retry. A leader that is not in its own configuration can neither count its own vote for a quorum it is not part of nor answer safely, so the receipt records whether such a request is answered, refused, or accepted and then dropped.
experiment.responsibility: raft (target): the MsgReadIndex path decides whether a leader that its own tracker shows is not in the configuration takes the request into a read-only round, and the path that ends its leadership decides what happens to a request it already accepted.

comparisons.description: Premise: after the removal node 1 still leads, but its configuration has two voters, so the singleton shortcut cannot decide this request.
Premise: the new leader of {2,3} has committed an entry the removed leader's commit index does not cover.
Premise: the removed leader accepts the request into readOnly.unconfirmedReads, broadcasts its heartbeats and answers nothing.
Bound: one heartbeat tick is enough for the removed leader to learn of the new term and leave the leader state.

Witness: the request the removed leader accepted is never answered - no read state, no unconfirmed or pending request left behind, and no refusal handed to the caller, so its only recourse is its own retry deadline.

scope.description: Observe the whole interval of one postponed ReadIndex request on a real 4-node group: the leader postpones it, the application then applies an already-committed configuration change whose resulting configuration commits the leader's first entry of the term, the acknowledgement of the previous configuration arrives late, a heartbeat round runs, and finally an unrelated proposal is committed.
assumptions: Four voters {1,2,3,4} bootstrapped from a ConfState-only snapshot, with log entries 1..9 ordinary and entry 10 the configuration change, HardState{Term:1, Commit:10}, applied index 10 (the application has reported applied progress but has not yet called ApplyConfChange for entry 10, which node.go:166-187 permits).

Transport preserves raft's per-message semantics (each message is Stepped by its target and resulting messages are delivered in order); voters are reachable for votes; voter 4 is unreachable and voter 3's append acknowledgements are delayed, which is the message-loss/delay part of the fault model.
The applied change is taken from the log entry at index 10 exactly as an application does when it applies CommittedEntries.
excluded: Pre-vote, check-quorum and lease-based reads (all disabled by the test configuration stub).
Snapshot-based recovery and asynchronous storage writes.

basis.prefix: For each case: build four nodes whose storage is bootstrapped with the case ConfState (voters {1,2,3,4}, or the joint configuration voters {1,2,3} + voters_outgoing {1,2,3,4}), append ten term-1 entries with entry 10 the case configuration change, persist HardState{Term:1,Commit:10} and set Applied=10; then elect node 1 with a real MsgHup/MsgVote/MsgVoteResp round (voter 4 unreachable, voter 3's MsgAppResp delayed), deliver the client's MsgReadIndex, apply the committed change at index 10 via applyConfChange, deliver the delayed acknowledgement, run one heartbeat round (tick), and finally propose one unrelated entry.
basis.requirement: A ReadIndex request that a leader accepts by postponing (raft.go:1363-1368) must be answered once the leader has committed an entry of its term, whichever path performs that commit (raft.go:1550-1554 for the MsgAppResp path, raft.go:2013-2028 for the switchToConfig path), because the helper that discharges the duty is guarded only by committedEntryInCurrentTerm() (raft.go:2127-2145) and the caller's comment states the release is due once the committed index has progressed for the term.
basis.responsibility: raft (target): the leader is the producer of the answer for a request it accepted, and switchToConfig is part of raft, not of the application.

comparisons.description: Precondition observation: the leader postponed the received request because no entry of its term was committed (committed_entry_term 1, leader_term 2).

Witness: applying the committed removal of voter 4 performed the leader's first commit of term 2 (committed 10 -> 11, committed_entry_term 2 == leader_term), so the postponed request is due to be answered, but it is still pending and no ReadState was produced.
Variant of the same cause: applying the committed zero change left the joint configuration, so the incoming half committed the leader's first term-2 entry, yet the postponed request is still pending.

No repair from the periodic round: two heartbeats are sent with an empty read context (heartbeat_ctx_len 0), the delayed acknowledgement of the previous configuration is already in place (match_3 11), and no ReadState is produced.

Control: an unrelated proposal committed by the new configuration releases the postponed request (released_request_ctx A), so the release mechanism works and is reached only through the MsgAppResp commit path.
Control for the joint variant: the postponed request is only released once the unrelated proposal is committed.

scope.description: Observe what raft answers for a ReadIndex request that arrives at a node which the application removed from its configuration while it was leading (StepDownOnRemoval false), after the remaining voter has become leader of the reduced single-voter configuration and committed an entry the removed leader never receives.
assumptions: Two voters {1,2} in one process, ReadOnlySafe, default Config (StepDownOnRemoval false, CheckQuorum false, PreVote false).
Node 1 is elected leader, then the application proposes and applies the committed configuration change that removes node 1 on both nodes.
Node 2 campaigns and commits one entry; no message from the current configuration reaches node 1 (its heartbeats at the old term are ignored by node 2 because CheckQuorum and PreVote are disabled).
excluded: Check-quorum and pre-vote configurations, which give a leader another way to learn that it is stale.
Snapshot transfer and asynchronous storage writes.

comparisons.description: The node whose removal the application applied is still leading, with a configuration whose single voter is another node (singleton true, is_voter false).
The actual leader of the reduced configuration has committed an entry that the removed leader's commit index does not cover (committed 4 vs 2).

Witness: the removed leader answered the ReadIndex request with index 2, below the commit index 4 the actual leader already had, without sending any message (heartbeats_emitted 0, messages_emitted empty, pending_reads 0).

Control: the same request answered by the node that is the actual leader of the configuration returns an index that covers its commit index, so the local singleton answer is only unsafe on the node that is no longer the voter.

No repair from the periodic path: after three heartbeat intervals and no replies from the current configuration, the removed leader is still leading at its old term and still answers with the same stale index.

basis.requirement: Node.Propose is the application-facing proposal path: its documentation states that it proposes data to be appended to the log and warns only that proposals can be lost without notice (node.go:138-140). basis.responsibility: raft (target): the wrapper's own bookkeeping decides whether the application's proposals reach the group, and the target's comment at node.go:409-411 records that this bookkeeping is unsound.

scope.description: Observe a postponed ReadIndex request through the Node interface of a wrapped leader whose application has reported applied progress past a committed configuration change without having applied it yet, and then applies that change: the decisive observation is whether any Ready delivers the ReadState for the request once the leader has committed an entry of its term.
assumptions: The wrapped node 1 is a four-voter group {1,2,3,4} whose storage holds ten term-1 entries with the last one removing voter 4, and a persisted HardState committing index 10.

Voter 2 is a bare raft instance whose acknowledgements are delivered; voter 3 is a bare raft instance whose append acknowledgements are held (delayed), and voter 4 is unreachable, so the leader cannot commit under the configuration it still has.

The application consumes Readys, writes entries, hard state and snapshots to the leader's storage, calls Advance (reported applied progress through index 10) and only later calls ApplyConfChange for the change it observed; the campaign and the ReadIndex request are issued through the Node interface.

basis.prefix: Build the wrapped leader over the four-voter fixture, pump its Readys (persisting buffers and calling Advance) without calling ApplyConfChange so that applied index 10 is reported while the tracker still holds voters=(1 2 3 4); campaign through the Node interface and pump until it reports StateLeader at term 2 with its term entry acknowledged only by voter 2; issue ReadIndex with context A and pump; then call ApplyConfChange for the committed removal of voter 4 and pump, recording every ReadState the Readys deliver.

assumptions: Four voters {1,2,3,4} bootstrapped from a ConfState-only snapshot, log entries 1..9 ordinary and entry 10 the configuration change, HardState{Term:1, Commit:10}, applied index 10 (the application reported applied progress but has not yet called ApplyConfChange for entry 10, which node.go:166-187 permits).

scope.description: Observe the removed-leader ReadIndex path in four configurations of the same removal: a single-voter remainder, a two-voter remainder, a single-voter remainder with CheckQuorum enabled, and a single-voter remainder with PreVote enabled and CheckQuorum disabled.
assumptions: Scenarios in one process: voters {1,2} where the removal leaves {2}; voters {1,2,3} where the removal leaves {2,3}; and voters {1,2} with Config.CheckQuorum true on both nodes; ReadOnlySafe and StepDownOnRemoval false in all of them.

In each scenario node 1 is elected leader, the application proposes and applies the committed removal of node 1 on every node, the remaining voters then elect node 2 and commit one entry, and only then is the ReadIndex request delivered to node 1.

In the CheckQuorum scenario the observations are taken before and after the first heartbeat tick of the removed leader, so the receipt covers both the window in which the stale answer is issued and the state after the step-down.

In the PreVote scenario the observations are taken before and after the first heartbeat tick of the removed leader, as in the CheckQuorum scenario, so the receipt covers the window in which the stale answer is issued and the state after the step-down.
excluded: Snapshot transfer and asynchronous storage writes.

basis.prefix: Scenario A (single-voter remainder): elect node 1 in {1,2}, apply the committed removal of node 1, elect node 2 in {2} and commit one proposal, deliver MsgReadIndex to node 1, deliver the same request to node 2, run three heartbeat intervals on node 1 and deliver a second MsgReadIndex to node 1. Scenario B (two-voter remainder): elect node 1 in {1,2,3}, apply the committed removal on all three nodes, elect node 2 in {2,3} and commit one proposal, deliver MsgReadIndex to node 1, then run three heartbeat intervals on node 1. Scenario C (single-voter remainder with CheckQuorum): as scenario A with Config.CheckQuorum true, but the read is delivered before the removed leader has contacted the new leader, then one heartbeat tick is delivered and the step-down is observed, then a further MsgReadIndex is delivered. Scenario D (single-voter remainder with PreVote and without CheckQuorum): as scenario C, but the read is delivered before the removed leader has contacted the new leader, then one heartbeat tick is delivered and the step-down is observed, then a further MsgReadIndex is delivered.
basis.requirement: A ReadIndex answer must let the application serve a linearizable read (raft.go:233-244 and README.md:27-32 state that ReadOnlySafe achieves linearizability by communicating with the quorum, and node.go:218-224 states that once the application advances past the returned read index, linearizable reads issued before the request can be processed safely). The tracker's own comment for IsSingleton says the single voting member is the leader, so answering locally without any check is only sound when that member is the local node.
basis.responsibility: raft (target): the singleton shortcut in the ReadIndex path decides the answer for the whole configuration, and the library already refuses proposals from a leader that is not in its own configuration.

comparisons.description: Scenario A premise: the node whose removal the application applied is still leading a configuration whose single voter is another node.
Scenario A premise: the actual leader of the reduced configuration has committed an entry the removed leader's commit index does not cover.
Scenario A witness: the removed leader answered the read with an index below the commit index of the actual leader, sending no message at all.
Scenario A control: the same request answered by the actual leader returns an index that covers its commit index.
Scenario A persistence: after three heartbeat intervals without replies the removed leader repeats the same stale index.
Scenario B premise: the same removal leaves a configuration with two voters, so the singleton shortcut cannot apply to the removed leader (config voters=(2 3)).
Scenario B premise: the new leader of {2,3} has committed an entry the removed leader's commit index does not cover.

Scenario B control outcome: the same read delivered to the removed leader produces no answer at all, and the leader instead enters the readOnly round (heartbeats_emitted 2 with a read context) - the stale immediate answer is specific to the singleton configuration.

Scenario B second symptom: the accepted read stays in readOnly.unconfirmed_reads because the current configuration never acknowledges the removed leader's old-term heartbeats, so no repair exists for it inside raft.
Scenario B persistence: three further heartbeat intervals still produce no answer and no reply from the current configuration.
Scenario C premise: with CheckQuorum enabled the removal still leaves node 1 leading a configuration whose single voter is node 2, so the shortcut applies.
Scenario C premise: the new leader of {2} has committed an entry the removed leader's commit index does not cover.
Scenario C witness before the step-down: enabling CheckQuorum does not remove the stale answer - the removed leader still answers with index 2 below the committed index 4 of the actual leader.
Scenario C mitigation: the current leader answers the removed leader's old-term heartbeat with its higher term, so the removed leader becomes a follower (lead None) after one heartbeat tick.
Scenario C bound: the stale-answer window is at most the heartbeat interval - one tick was enough for the step-down in the exercised configuration.
Scenario C after the step-down: the same request is no longer answered (it is dropped because the node has no leader), so the exposure is bounded by the step-down rather than repaired inside raft.
PreVote premise: the removal still leaves node 1 leading a configuration whose single voter is node 2, so the shortcut applies.
PreVote premise: the new leader of {2} has committed an entry the removed leader's commit index does not cover.
PreVote witness before the step-down: with PreVote only the removed leader still answers with index 2 below the committed index 4 of the actual leader.
PreVote bound: one heartbeat tick is enough for the step-down, matching the guard (checkQuorum || preVote) on messages from a lower term.
PreVote after the step-down: the same request is no longer answered, so PreVote alone bounds the exposure as the source predicts.

scope.description: Observe the whole interval of one postponed ReadIndex request for two completion paths on the same 4-node group: a local request answered into leader 1's readStates, and a forwarded request (client to follower 2, follower forwards to leader 1) whose answer must be a MsgReadIndexResp delivered back to node 2. In both paths the application then applies an already-committed configuration change whose resulting configuration performs the leader's first commit of the term.
assumptions: Four voters {1,2,3,4} bootstrapped from a ConfState-only snapshot, log entries 1..9 ordinary and entry 10 the configuration change, HardState{Term:1, Commit:10}, applied index 10 (the application reported applied progress but has not yet called ApplyConfChange for entry 10, which node.go:166-187 permits).
Transport preserves raft's per-message semantics; voter 4 is unreachable and voter 3's append acknowledgements are delayed (message loss/delay).
The forwarded request is produced by delivering MsgReadIndex without a From to follower 2, so follower 2 forwards it to the leader it knows, exactly as the Node.ReadIndex path does.
excluded: Snapshot-based recovery and asynchronous storage writes.

basis.prefix: For each case: build four nodes whose storage is bootstrapped with the case ConfState (voters {1,2,3,4}, or the joint configuration voters {1,2,3} + voters_outgoing {1,2,3,4}), append ten term-1 entries with entry 10 the case configuration change, persist HardState{Term:1,Commit:10} and set Applied=10; elect node 1 with a real MsgHup/MsgVote/MsgVoteResp round (voter 4 unreachable, voter 3's MsgAppResp delayed); deliver the read request (locally to node 1, or to follower 2 which forwards it); apply the committed change at index 10 via applyConfChange; deliver the delayed acknowledgement; run one heartbeat round (tick); finally propose one unrelated entry.

basis.responsibility: raft (target): the leader is the producer of the answer for a request it accepted, and switchToConfig is part of raft, not of the application.

comparisons.description: Precondition observation: the leader postponed the received request because no entry of its term was committed (committed_entry_term 1, leader_term 2).

No repair from the periodic round: two heartbeats are sent with an empty read context (heartbeat_ctx_len 0), the delayed acknowledgement of the previous configuration is already in place (match_3 11), and no ReadState is produced.

Control: an unrelated proposal committed by the new configuration releases the postponed request (released_request_ctx A), so the release mechanism works and is reached only through the MsgAppResp commit path.
Control for the joint variant: the postponed request is only released once the unrelated proposal is committed.
Forwarded-path premise: follower 2 (StateFollower, known leader 1) emits MsgReadIndex addressed to leader 1, so the answer owed is a MsgReadIndexResp to node 2.
Forwarded-path premise: the leader postponed the forwarded request because no entry of its term was committed.

Forwarded-path witness: applying the committed change performed the leader's first commit of term 2 (committed 10 -> 11, committed_entry_term 2 == leader_term) yet no MsgReadIndexResp was emitted and follower 2 received no ReadState, so the client's forwarded read stays unanswered.
Forwarded-path control: the unrelated proposal committed by the new configuration releases the postponed request, and only then does follower 2 receive the MsgReadIndexResp (ctx A, index 12).

scope.description: Observe the forwarded route into the same missing membership check. assumptions: The initial group has voters {1,2} and learner 3 (withLearners(3)), PreVote is enabled on every node and CheckQuorum is disabled, the election tick is 10 and the heartbeat tick is 1, and node 1 is elected with a real MsgHup/MsgPreVote/MsgVote round so that every node, the learner included, knows node 1 as its leader.

The learner's application issues the read while node 1 is still the leader it knows, so raft forwards the request to node 1; the forwarded request and its answer are delivered by hand after the removal has been applied, standing for a delay that outlasts the reconfiguration.
The messages of node 2 are drained rather than delivered, so the requester has not yet heard from the new leader and still routes its read to node 1.
